keyVerseText: And there will I nourish thee; for yet there are five years of famine; lest thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast, come to poverty.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb כּוּל (kûwl) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the idea of containing, measuring, or sustaining. Its core sense involves the capacity to hold or support something, whether physically or figuratively. This root meaning extends beyond the simple English gloss of 'can' or 'be able to,' emphasizing the action of maintaining or nourishing, which enriches our understanding of God's provision and care in Scripture.
usageInScripture: Across its 37 occurrences, כּוּל is consistently used to express the concepts of sustaining, nourishing, and making provision. The top translations such as 'and fed,' 'cannot contain,' and 'made provision' highlight its versatile application in contexts of physical nourishment and capacity. This range reveals that the word often relates to God's sustaining power and the ability to provide or hold in, underscoring a theme of divine support and care.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, כּוּל captures a vital aspect of God's character as a sustainer and nourisher of His people. Understanding this word helps believers grasp that God's providence is not merely about ability but about active, ongoing support and maintenance of life. It reflects the dependable and nurturing nature of God who provides for His creation in every circumstance. This word also reminds Christians of the spiritual sustenance offered through Christ, who upholds and nourishes His followers continually.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 45:11, the phrase 'And there will I nourish thee' uses כּוּל to convey God's provision during a time of famine. This word emphasizes not just survival but active nourishment and care, assuring that despite hardship, God will sustain Joseph and his household. It reassures believers that God's provision is intentional and sufficient, preventing poverty through His sustaining grace.
